title: Semi-Automated Discovery of Structural Elements Controlling GPCR Function.
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该文开发半自动化分析流程，对GPCR分子模拟轨迹进行无监督聚类并识别关键结构元件，虽为工程化应用且方法创新有限，但聚焦蛋白构象变化与功能机制，与蛋白质结构计算模拟课题直接相关。
abstract: Molecular simulations of G-protein-coupled receptors have become an important part of the structural biology toolkit, revealing structure-function mechanisms that are unobservable from experimental structures alone. With the advance of hardware and software, it has become routine to obtain trajectories that are tens of microseconds in duration, opening new opportunities for yet more rigorous and reproducible observations on mechanism. Toward this end, we presented a semi-automated analysis pipeline which operates on featurized simulation data, performs unsupervised clustering, and then identifies which input features are most discriminatory of cluster identity. Application of this pipeline to a large set of G-protein-coupled receptor simulation data shows that it identifies several well-known microswitches. Inspection of these structural elements reveals changes in conformation that are known to accompany functional transitions of the receptor. In addition to these known structural elements, the analysis also identifies functional transitions associated with one new motif horizontal line the kink in transmembrane helix 2 horizontal line and discovers a coupled "piston-like" motion of TM2 and TM3 that elaborates a previously reported motion of TM3.
abstract_zh: G蛋白偶联受体的分子模拟已成为结构生物学工具箱中的重要组成部分，揭示了仅凭实验结构无法观察到的结构-功能机制。随着硬件和软件的发展，获得持续数十微秒的轨迹已成为常规操作，为更严谨且可重复的机制观察开辟了新机遇。为此，我们提出了一种半自动分析流程，该流程对特征化模拟数据进行操作，执行无监督聚类，并识别哪些输入特征最能区分聚类身份。将此流程应用于大型G蛋白偶联受体模拟数据集，表明它能识别出多个已知的微开关。对这些结构元件的检查揭示了伴随受体功能转变而发生的构象变化。除这些已知结构元件外，分析还识别出与一个新基序——跨膜螺旋2中的扭结——相关的功能转变，并发现TM2和TM3的耦合“活塞样”运动，这详细阐述了先前报道的TM3运动。
